extracted.intended_audience: policymakers, finance ministers, statesmen, and informed readers interested in public finance and fiscal policy
extracted.subtask_description: Principles and practical standards for managing state revenue, public credit, and fiscal institutions (criticisms of French Revolutionary finance). Focuses on what makes sound public finance and what constitutes malpractice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objects of a financier
rubrics_metrics.description: “The objects of a financier are, then, to secure an ample revenue; to impose it with judgment and equality; to employ it economically; and, when necessity obliges him, to make use of credit.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This lists the core duties against which a finance minister should be judged: sufficiency of revenue, fairness of taxation, economical expenditure, and prudent use of credit only when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foundations of public finance (transparency and soundness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Finance should rest “in the clearness and candour of [its] proceedings, the exactness of [its] calculations, and the solidity of [its] funds.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Officials must present transparent accounts, accurate estimates, and rely on solid funds rather than artifice. Openness and exact calculation are prerequisites to lasting credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain proper balance between private and public claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Prosperity increases when “the balance between what is left to strengthen the efforts of individuals, and what is collected for the common efforts of the state, bear to each other a due reciprocal proportion.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Taxation and public appropriation must preserve incentives for private wealth creation; excessive or ill-proportioned extraction undermines both private and public prosperity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid destroying existing revenue sources without real replacements
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not decry or abolish established revenue systems unless you have a practicable plan to replace them; commissioners should be tried by the plain duty of a common finance minister rather than ideal models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticizes rhetorical denunciation of old systems (e.g., salt monopoly) followed by failure to provide enforceable, equitable replacements — such actions lead to revenue collapse and disorder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equality and proportionality in taxation
rubrics_metrics.description: Impositions must be “proportioned to the means of the citizens, and the least likely to lean heavy on the active capital employed in the generation of private wealth.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tax schemes should be designed to be fair and avoid disproportionately burdening productive capital; local bargaining or patchwork measures risk creating new, oppressive inequalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not rely on voluntary contributions as a stable revenue source
rubrics_metrics.description: Voluntary benevolences are “a tax weak, ineffective, and unequal; a tax by which luxury, avarice, and selfishness were screened, and the load thrown upon productive capital… a tax of regulation upon virtue.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voluntary levies are unreliable, distort incentives, and conceal social inequities; they should not substitute for systematic taxation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prudent use and prerequisites of paper money / bank-paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Paper should have its origin in cash actually deposited, be convertible at pleasure, and be accepted by choice — our paper is of value in commerce because 'in law it is of none.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Currency issued by the state or banks must be backed by real deposits or convertible into coin; forced acceptance or legal compulsion undermines credit and trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject issuing inconvertible paper as a substitute for real revenue
rubrics_metrics.description: Issuing successive batches of assignats (paper money) to cover deficits is condemned — when old assignats depreciate the remedy proposed is merely to issue new assignats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Printing more unbacked paper to cover shortfalls produces depreciation and undermines revenue collection; it is a self-defeating practice that destroys public credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for establishing a land-bank (using property as security)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before offering land as security: ascertain the gross value of the estate; the charges of its management and disposition; the perpetual and temporary incumbrances; strike a net surplus (the only security); properly vest it in trustees; specify parcels, time and conditions of sale; then allow public subscription or assignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lays out a methodical, businesslike procedure for converting land into a credible fund: full valuation, clear accounting of charges/incumbrances, legal vesting, and clear terms — otherwise the security is illusory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Openness, candour, and authentication of confiscated-property securities
rubrics_metrics.description: If church or confiscated lands are to be used as security, there must be an open and exact statement of their clear value, inventories of moveable effects, and disclosure of charges so the estate may be 'disengaged of all charges.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using confiscated property as a fund requires authenticating values and liabilities immediately; failure to do so amounts to fraud and destroys confidence in the instrument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account fully for additional expenses created by reforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Economy must consider the Assembly’s own expenses, municipalities, armies, police, new judicatures, and pension lists — comparing present costs to former revenues reveals true economy or extravagance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fiscal reformers must not claim saved expense without accounting for all new institutional and administrative costs created by reforms; otherwise claimed economy is illusory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not base public credit on confiscation or sacrilege
rubrics_metrics.description: The attempt to destroy settled revenue in hope of rebuilding it with the materials of confiscated property is condemned: 'Never did a state, in any case, enrich itself by the confiscations of the citizens.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confiscation may supply short-term resources but does not create sustainable credit or prosperity; relying on spoliation is economically and morally destructive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credit requires voluntary confidence, not coercion
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign merchants and bankers will not deal with a people who 'attempt to reverse the very nature of things' or where the debtor prescribes terms at bayonet-point; credit cannot be commanded by force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legitimacy and predictability are prerequisites for external credit; coercive or revolutionary acts that undermine property rights and enforce terms by force repel willing lenders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid creating fictitious representations of wealth
rubrics_metrics.description: When treasuries 'sinks every day more in cash, and swells more and more in fictitious representation' the state mistakes paper for real prosperity; representative money must be convertible and rooted in real commerce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Skeptical standard for evaluating money supply and paper instruments: check convertibility, origin, and whether paper facilitates circulation because it stands on real coin/commerce rather than replacing it.
